External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0113-0048 showed the wellhead at 30.3 °C with the air at 26.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 3 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).

  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0113-030

Asset: WELL-0113 (NE-07 Well 113, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 19 Jun 2026 08:00 · Finished: 20 Jun 2026 02:00 · Well stopped for this job: 18 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0113-0191 on 2026-06-18 Report written: 21 Jun 2026

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0113-0191 at 08:30 on 2026-06-18 found crude oil on the pad: about 5.4% of the pad area, estimated 3.1 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.4 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged. This is corrective repair number 4 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level; one crew member's monitor had not been bump-tested that day (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 251 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 201 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 1.9 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0113-030 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.33% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Notes and recommendations

  • Inspect the remaining joints on this flowline.
  • Record the leak location for the flowline maintenance program (RC-05).
  • Start a root-cause analysis for this equipment before the next repair is closed (well-type manual, section 10).
  • HSE to follow up on the WS-03 item above with the crew.
